## The tracer flux positivity limiter (`equation-of-state/limiter`) {#sec-ch08-theta}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md chapter 8, scheme 8.1
status: draft

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Scales each face's tracer flux by a factor of the cell it drains, so no cell is emptied past zero.
- Switch: `equation-of-state/limiter`, default false, and only where there are tracer rows.
- Acts on tracer channels only. Density and pressure get floors, not a limiter.
- Exactly conservative, because both cells of a face use the same factor.
- Inactive where a cell can afford its outflow, so the high-order flux is untouched almost everywhere.
:::

This is the only mechanism in snapy that *guarantees* anything about positivity, and it guarantees it
for tracers alone. For each cell and species it computes the largest uniform scaling of that cell's
outgoing fluxes that cannot drain it below zero in one forward-Euler step, then applies the factor of
the donor cell to every face. It runs inside the stage operator of @sec-ch04-divergence, after the
seam averaging of @sec-ch04-seam and before the flux divergence.

### Derivation

Charge each cell for what leaves it. Summing the outgoing part of $AF$ over the cell's faces,

$$
\mathrm{out}_i = \sum_{f} \max(\pm A_f F_f,\, 0),\qquad
\theta_i = \min\!\left(1,\ \frac{u_i V_i}{\Delta t\,\mathrm{out}_i}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch08-theta-def}

with the sign chosen so that only genuinely outgoing contributions count: inflow is not charged.
Applying $\theta$ of the donor cell to every face then gives $u_i + \Delta t\,\Delta u_i \ge 0$ cell by
cell.

`[C1]` checks the guarantee on the state rather than on the formula. Over four thousand random flux
fields the unlimited update drives some cell negative in every one, worst $-5.879$; the limited update
never does, worst exactly $0$. The check computes the divergence independently of the limiter, so it
measures the result and not the construction.

Two properties are worth separating, because they are easy to conflate and the chapter is more useful
if they are kept apart.

*Where the limiter acts.* `[C2]` finds that every one of the $25\,974$ cells that can afford their
outflow keeps $\theta = 1$ bitwise, and that no cell which cannot afford it was left unlimited. The
scheme is therefore not a smoothing: away from depletion the high-order flux passes through untouched.

*Why it conserves.* The conservation does **not** come from the donor rule. It comes from both cells of
a face seeing one number, so that the face cancels when the divergence is summed. `[C3]` separates
these: on a closed block the limited tendency sums to $1.7\times10^{-16}$ of the flux scale, while a
per-cell limiter, in which each cell scales only its own outflow and its neighbour does not agree,
leaks $8.5\times10^{-1}$. Any single factor per face telescopes; the donor rule is what buys positivity,
and `[C7]` checks that rule separately on forty-six thousand faces.

The step is limited at the full $\Delta t$ even inside a multi-stage integrator, and that is sound
because of how the shipped integrators are built. `[C5]` reads their weights rather than assuming
them: each stage is $w_0 U^n + w_1(U + \alpha\,\Delta U)$ with $w_0 + w_1 = 1$ and $\alpha = w_2/w_1
\le 1$, a convex combination of a state already known non-negative and a damped full-step Euler update.

(b) The donor rule: the face takes the factor of the cell it drains, the lower cell where the flux is positive (green) and the upper cell otherwise (blue). Both cells of the face see that one number, which is what makes the scaling conservative."

The factors are built by `flux_positivity_theta` at [`flux_positivity.cpp:22-72`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L22-L72). The
outgoing sum is accumulated over exactly the faces the divergence will consume, with a pair of
rectified terms per direction at `slice` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:39-47`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L39-L47)), so the limiter and the
divergence cannot disagree about which face drains which cell.

Two details of that function matter to a reader. The available mass stops a little short of zero, at
`margin` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:63-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L63-L66)), because an exact-zero target rounds negative; that margin is
@sec-ch08-roundoff. And ghost cells are given $\theta = 1$ here, because their outflow is never
accumulated: the caller must fill the ghost layer the way conserved variables are filled before
scaling, or the two ranks sharing a face would apply different factors and conservation would fail.

The scaling is `flux_positivity_scale_` at [`flux_positivity.cpp:74-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L74-L104), which selects the
donor per face with a `where` on the sign of the flux. The call site is
`narrow` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:648-669`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L648-L669)), which also keeps the census that
@sec-ch08-roundoff describes, and the ghost fill it depends on follows at
`pmb` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:671-686`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L671-L686)), a raw copy that is never interpolated because an interpolated
ghost is not the neighbour's factor.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Tracers only. Nothing here keeps dry density or pressure positive; those have floors
  (@sec-ch08-eoslimiter) and a redo detector (@sec-ch08-redo), and neither is a guarantee.
- The guarantee is per stage, for transport only. A source term, a sedimentation flux added after the
  limiter, or the implicit solve can still drive a tracer negative.
:::

1. **The ghost fill is a precondition, not a check.** If a caller scales before filling $\theta$'s ghost
   layer, the two ranks of a seam face apply different factors and conservation breaks silently. The
   code says so in its header; nothing asserts it at runtime.
2. **Hypothesis, not measured here.** That limiting at the full $\Delta t$ is enough for the multi-stage
   update rests on the convex-combination argument `[C5]` verifies for the shipped weights. It is an
   argument about the weights, not a measurement of a multi-stage run; no check in this chapter
   integrates a full Runge-Kutta step.
